what_it_states: Sections 1-2: DP definition, sensitivity space S_T, K-norm sensitivity, K-norm mechanism (Prop 2.8, density proportional to exp(-(eps/Delta)||v||_K)), Example 2.10. Section 3: containment and volume orders on K-norm mechanisms only; stochastic tightness (Def 3.3, Thm 3.6), depth (Thm 3.11, Cor 3.12), entropy (Prop 3.14, Thm 3.15), conditional variance given a direction (Lemma 3.16, Thm 3.17), optimal K-mech = convex hull of S_T (Lemma 3.18, Thm 3.19), Examples 3.20/3.22. Section 4: extended objective perturbation (Algorithm 2, Thm 4.1) and logistic-regression simulations. Section 5: functional-mechanism linear regression, sensitivity hulls K2/K3, simulations and housing data. Section 6: discussion and a Monte Carlo cautionary example showing that containment within K-norm mechanisms does not imply smaller marginal variance or expected l_inf/l_2/l_1 loss. Section 7: samplers (Algorithms 5-8) and proofs (Lemmas 7.2-7.3, proofs of Lemma 3.4/3.5/3.16, Thm 3.6/3.11/3.17/4.1, Prop 3.14). Related work cites Geng-Viswanath 2013 (two-dimensional correlated staircase minimizing expected l1 loss) and Geng-Viswanath 2015 (scalar l1/l2).
what_it_does_not_state: No statement over ALL additive noise laws (every optimality result is within the K-norm exponential family); no squared-Euclidean (MSE) optimality or selector even within the family (the paper deliberately uses intrinsic containment/volume orders and warns, Remark 3.7 and Section 6, that expected-loss rankings depend on the loss and scaling); no l1-diamond sensitivity squared-Euclidean all-law value, selector or equality; no staircase optimizer; no mixed-cost all-law bound E||Z||_2^2 >= (2/3) inf E||Z||_1^2; no rounded-core selector.
